Sub: Revised delegation of financial powers to Section Supervisors (SS) for settlement
of claims.

Ref: HO circular of even number dated 05.03.2012 and circular No.
Manual/Amendment/2011/pt/1948 dated 01.05.2017 ((on EPFO website at Sl. No.
584 for 2011-12 and at SI. No. 47 for 2017-18 on ‘office orders/ circulars’).

Sir,

After introduction of Composite Claim Forms and smooth processing of the same, the
Central P.F. Commissioner in exercise of Powers conferred upon him under para 24(3) of the
EPF Scheme, 1952 has revised the following delegation of Financial Powers for authorization
of claims and the same are to be implemented after necessary modification in the application
software: -

2 Settlement of claims in respect of Composite Claim Form (Aadhar/Non-Aadhar)
including Composite Claim Form in death cases and in respect of Form-13 (Un-exempted) &
Form-14 (LIP Payment), the following delegation has been made -:

a) Claim will be submitted by DA (Accounts) and approved by SS (Claims) in case the
settlement amount is up to Rs. 50,000 /-i ing i i

b) Claim will be submitted by DA (Accounts) and approved by AO (Accounts) where
claim settlement amount is more than Rs. 50,000/-(operative accounts).

c) In case of settlement of claims out of inoperative accounts, claim will be submitted
by DA (Accounts) and approved by AO (Accounts) if the settlement amount is more
than Rs. 50,000/- but less than Rs. 1,00,000/-.

d) Incase of settlement of claims out of inoperative accounts, claim will be submitted
by DA (Accounts) and approved by APFC if the settlement amount is beyond Rs.
1,00,000/-.

a. Form 10C (Scheme Certificate Cases only) and Form-10D (Input Data Sheet)- Claim
will be submitted by DA (Accounts) and approved by AO (Accounts).

4. Form-13 (Exempted): Claim will be submitted by DA (Accounts) and will be approved
by SS (Claims).

5. The return/rejection of claims: DA (Accounts) will submit the return/rejection and
APFC (Accounts) will approve it.

6. However, in case of a claim where the amount for approval rests with two different
levels under two schemes, then the claim shall be settled by higher of the two authorities and
the same shall be applied uniformly for settlement of all type of claims.

(This issues with the approval of Central P.F. Commissioner).

Yours faithfully,

Ld te
(Udita Chowdhary )

Addl. Central P.F. Commissioner (F&A)
